scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Apanomeritis originates in Crete, Greece. It was performed in central regions like Rethymno and Heraklion until shortly after the war.
Historically a mixed dance for men and women, it is now danced mainly by women.
on_screen: Map: Greece · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is also called provatinistikos, or 'sheep dance'. The stamping footwork mimics sheep when they are agitated or nervous.
It was a communal dance until shortly after the war and continues today through women's performances.
It is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Onze Slag (Adhunik Hanpuriyan Album) (https://archive.org/details/onze-slag-adhunik-hanpuriyan-album)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers form a circle.
They hold hands palm-to-palm with arms crossed down.
The ten-step pattern includes stamps against the ground, imitating the movements of nervous sheep.
Watch for the Provatinistikos stamp.
